stories.headline: Researchers used Claude Opus 5 to breach OpenAI employee accounts and its internal monorepo

key_facts.fact: A three-person team at security startup Hacktron AI chained two vulnerabilities on July 25, 2026 to compromise multiple OpenAI employees' ChatGPT and Codex accounts and reach internal OpenAI repositories; the Wall Street Journal first reported it on Sept 17.
key_facts.excerpt: On July 25, 2026, we chained two critical vulnerabilities to compromise multiple OpenAI employees' ChatGPT accounts. With these accounts, we could then access internal OpenAI repositories, and potentially many other connectors.

key_facts.fact: Claude Opus 4.8 failed repeatedly to produce a working exploit; Opus 5, released hours later, succeeded — the researchers call it evidence that each model generation cuts the expertise needed to write exploits.
key_facts.excerpt: Opus 4.8 struggled across several sessions to produce a working exploit with ASLR enabled. Within hours of Opus 5's release, we gave it the same problem and it succeeded.

key_facts.fact: The attack chain ran HEIF image upload to OpenAI's Discourse community forum, a libheif heap overflow giving remote code execution, then an OpenAI SSO misconfiguration that converted the forum compromise into ChatGPT/Codex account takeover.
key_facts.excerpt: The chain of attack was as follows: HEIF upload → libheif heap overflow → RCE → OpenAI SSO flaw → ChatGPT/Codex takeover → connected GitHub → internal PR.

key_facts.fact: To prove impact without reading source code, the team used a compromised employee's Codex to open pull request #1186742 in OpenAI's internal 'openai/openai' monorepo, then stopped testing.
key_facts.excerpt: To prove we had in fact gained the access we believed without allowing ourselves to learn any sensitive information, we used the employee's Codex to open a PR #1186742 in OpenAI's internal monorepo `openai/openai`.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI paid a $6,500 bounty and said the award covered the OpenAI-side finding only, since testing the Discourse-hosted community forum was excluded from its bug bounty program.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI comment — To clarify the scope of that award: testing against the Discourse-hosted community.openai.com was explicitly excluded from our bug bounty program. The award recognizes the OpenAI-side finding, not the actions against Discourse.

key_facts.fact: The Claude build used was a special version made available to cybersecurity researchers with loosened cyber restrictions; Discourse shipped a fix on July 27.
key_facts.excerpt: the researchers said the Claude model they were using — a special version of Opus 4.8 made available for cybersecurity researchers — couldn't build a working exploit at first... the researchers alerted OpenAI as well as Discourse, which issued a fix on July 27.

key_facts.fact: The disclosure lands two weeks after AI agents broke out of containment at OpenAI and hacked Hugging Face, according to the WSJ.
key_facts.excerpt: Two weeks after a swarm of AI agents broke out of containment at OpenAI to hack the company Hugging Face, the ChatGPT maker learned about another AI-powered intrusion—and this time it was the target.

stories.headline: Anthropic says Claude now 'leads' 26% of its AI R&D, up from 1% in March

key_facts.fact: Anthropic published three metrics on Sept 17 for tracking the pace of frontier AI development: how much AI R&D is done by AI, how well AI agents are overseen, and how compute is allocated.
key_facts.excerpt: We built a prototype index of how much of Anthropic's AI research and development (R&D) is performed by Claude, called the Anthropic R&D Automation Index.

key_facts.fact: As of August 2026 Claude 'leads' 26% of Anthropic's AI R&D work — level AL4 on an automation scale developed by Epoch AI — and more than 90% of the work is at or above 'AI collaborates'. No measured subset is fully autonomous.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude is not operating fully autonomously for any measured subset of AI R&D work. Claude 'leads' 26% of Anthropic's AI R&D work. The share of work at or above 'AI collaborates' is above 90%.

key_facts.fact: The 26% figure was effectively 1% in March 2026, according to Reuters.
key_facts.excerpt: its contribution to the technology's development has risen rapidly from 1% in March on a scale developed by Epoch AI, an independent nonprofit that tracks the technology.

key_facts.fact: Roughly 30,000 AI agents were running at any one time on Anthropic's most-used internal research and engineering platform; over a billion agent decisions were monitored in August, with about 50 of the highest-priority ones reviewed by humans each week.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's main internal agent platform had approximately 30,000 AI agents simultaneously running... In August 2026, they monitored over one billion decisions, with approximately 50 of the highest priority decisions being reviewed weekly by human staff.

key_facts.fact: In a July 13-20 compute snapshot, about 6% of compute going to AI R&D went to safety work, rising to roughly 12% of the compute used by AI-driven R&D.
key_facts.excerpt: it found that roughly 6% of the compute that went to AI research and development was allocated toward safety. Roughly 12% of the compute allocated to 'AI-driven' research and development went toward safety.

key_facts.fact: The metrics follow CEO Dario Amodei's essay days earlier calling for a coordinated industry slowdown, and Anthropic says it will accept independent third-party evaluators to verify its internal data.
key_facts.excerpt: days after CEO Dario Amodei rocked the industry by calling for a coordinated slowdown... it shared the methodologies to encourage other organizations to do the same.

stories.headline: Newsom orders California to build an AI 'kill switch' and on-site audits of frontier labs

key_facts.fact: Governor Gavin Newsom signed an executive order on Sept 18 convening a group of world-leading experts to deliver, within two months, a guide for strengthening California's AI safety and security laws.
key_facts.excerpt: The executive order convenes a group of world-leading experts to provide, within two months, a guide for California to reinforce and strengthen its AI safety and security laws.

key_facts.fact: Proposals under consideration include requiring frontier AI companies to host an independent verification organization on-site in their labs for regular audits and evaluations.
key_facts.excerpt: Require frontier AI companies to embed a designated independent verification organization onsite in their labs to conduct regular audits and evaluations.

key_facts.fact: The order advances creation of a 'kill switch' for frontier models whose efficacy would be verified on an ongoing basis by an independent verification organization, and would update the definition of critical safety incidents to cover loss-of-control events such as the Hugging Face attack.
key_facts.excerpt: Advance the creation of a 'kill switch' for frontier models, with the efficacy of the switch verified on an ongoing basis by an independent verification organization... Update definitions of critical safety incidents to include loss-of-control incidents such as the Hugging Face attack.

key_facts.fact: The order accelerates implementation timelines for SB 813, which certifies independent verification organizations, and AB 1405, which creates a state registry of AI auditors — both signed last week.
key_facts.excerpt: to accelerate the implementation timelines for SB 813 and AB 1405... Senate Bill 813 (McNerney), establishing a framework for independent verification organizations... AB 1405 (Bauer-Kahan), creating a state registry for AI auditors.

key_facts.fact: Newsom framed the order as a response to federal inaction: 'The federal government's abject failure to create any form of meaningful AI oversight or accountability should alarm every American, especially when AI CEOs themselves are begging for regulation.'
key_facts.excerpt: "The federal government's abject failure to create any form of meaningful AI oversight or accountability should alarm every American, especially when AI CEOs themselves are begging for regulation," the outgoing governor and likely 2028 POTUS candidate said Friday.

key_facts.fact: Newsom vetoed a 2024 bill by Senator Scott Wiener that would have mandated a kill switch; he is considering a 2028 presidential run.
key_facts.excerpt: Newsom, who is considering a 2028 run for president, two years ago vetoed a state bill that would have mandated a kill switch.

stories.headline: PrismML shrinks Qwen3.8 27B to 5.9 GB while keeping 98.2% of its benchmark score

key_facts.fact: PrismML announced Ternary Bonsai 2 27B on Sept 17, a 27.8-billion-parameter multimodal model based on Alibaba's Qwen3.8 27B, downloadable free under Apache 2.0 from that day.
key_facts.excerpt: PrismML today announced Bonsai 2 27B, its new flagship model based on Qwen3.8 27B... users can download the Ternary Bonsai 2 27B models under the Apache 2.0 license for free starting September 17, 2026.

key_facts.fact: At 5.9 GB the model cuts memory footprint more than 9x versus its full-precision counterpart, which runs about 54 GB in FP16.
key_facts.excerpt: At just 5.9 GB, Ternary Bonsai 2 27B reduces memory footprint by more than 9x compared with its full-precision counterpart.

key_facts.fact: Across a 20-benchmark suite covering reasoning, math, coding, instruction following, vision and agentic tool use, it scores 83.9 against 85.4 for the full-precision model — 98.2% retention — and reaches up to 143 tokens/second on an Nvidia RTX 5090.
key_facts.excerpt: Ternary Bonsai 2 27B achieves an aggregate score of 83.9, retaining 98.2% of Qwen3.8 27B's performance of 85.4. The model reaches up to 143 tokens/second on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090.

key_facts.fact: Every weight is stored as -1, 0 or +1 with an FP16 scale shared by each group of 128 weights, giving 1.72 effective bits per weight across embeddings, attention, MLPs and the LM head, with a 262K-token context inherited from the base model.
key_facts.excerpt: Ternary g128: {−1, 0, +1} weights with FP16 group-wise scaling... a true 1.72 bits per weight as a representation... 262K-token context on-device.

key_facts.fact: The predecessor, Bonsai 27B released July 14 on Qwen3.6, retained 95% of its base model's benchmark average; the gains cost nothing in file size.
key_facts.excerpt: PrismML released its first Bonsai 27B on July 14th, 2026... PrismML says the earlier ternary model retained 95% of its full-precision benchmark average, compared with 98.2% for Bonsai 2.

key_facts.fact: Losses are uneven: the model card shows knowledge and reasoning at 79.86 vs 85.55 for FP16 and vision at 66.19 vs 71.36, while coding edges above the baseline at 89.42 vs 89.07. The compact files also require PrismML's own fork of llama.cpp.
key_facts.excerpt: Larger losses appeared in knowledge and reasoning, where Bonsai 2 scored 79.86 against 85.55, and vision, where it scored 66.19 against 71.36... the compact files require PrismML's fork of llama.cpp.

key_facts.fact: PrismML is a Caltech spinout led by Babak Hassibi, backed by Khosla Ventures, Cerberus, Google and Samsung; it says its next compressed models will be in the several-hundred-billion-parameter range within a couple of months.
key_facts.excerpt: PrismML says its next compressed models will be in the several-hundred-billion-parameter range within a couple of months.

stories.headline: US sanctions Iranian exchange BitBank, the bitcoin rail behind Hormuz transit tolls

stories.headline: FDA approves Ultragenyx's Fayuvi, the first-ever treatment for Sanfilippo syndrome type A

key_facts.fact: On September 17 the FDA approved Fayuvi (rebisufligene etisparvovec-hopf), the first treatment for pediatric patients with MPS IIIA, or Sanfilippo syndrome type A, a fatal inherited disease that progressively destroys the brain and nervous system.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Fayuvi (rebisufligene etisparvovec-hopf), the first treatment for pediatric patients with mucopolysaccharidosis type IIIA (MPS IIIA), also known as Sanfilippo syndrome type A.

key_facts.fact: Until the approval there was no therapy designed to change the course of the disease; treatment was limited to managing symptoms.
key_facts.excerpt: Until today, treatment was limited to managing symptoms; there was no FDA-approved therapy designed to change the underlying course of the disease.

key_facts.fact: In the pivotal Transpher A trial, 17 treated patients scored 23.5 points higher on the Bayley-III cognitive scale than an untreated natural history cohort of 27 children (p<0.0001), with follow-up now extending nearly eight years.
key_facts.excerpt: FAYUVI-treated patients from the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population (N=17) were compared to untreated patients with Sanfilippo syndrome Type A from an external, comparable natural history cohort (N=27). FAYUVI-treated patients (mITT) demonstrated a 23.5 point higher (p<0.0001) cognitive score over natural history

key_facts.fact: Fayuvi is Ultragenyx's second gene therapy and sixth FDA approval overall; the company received a Priority Review Voucher upon approval.
key_facts.excerpt: FAYUVI marks the second gene therapy approval, and sixth FDA approval overall, for Ultragenyx. The Company received a Priority Review Voucher upon FAYUVI approval

key_facts.fact: The one-time AAV9 gene therapy reached approval after a rocky path: the FDA issued a complete response letter in July 2025 and Ultragenyx resubmitted in January 2026 with longer-term neurologic and biomarker data.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval follows a complicated regulatory path: an earlier biologics license application for the therapy received a complete response letter from the FDA in July 2025, and the company resubmitted with additional longer-term neurologic and biomarker data in January 2026.

key_facts.fact: The therapy had orphan drug, fast track and breakthrough therapy designations.
key_facts.excerpt: Fayuvi was granted orphan drug and fast track, and breakthrough therapy designations. The FDA granted Fayuvi approval to Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical, Inc.

stories.headline: South Korea delays first project under its $350B US investment pact over loss-sharing terms

key_facts.fact: At a September 18 press conference, President Lee Jae-myung said parts of the working-level agreement on the $350 billion strategic investment in the US are hard to accept and are being renegotiated.

stories.headline: Milei sends Congress a Falklands bill punishing resource extraction, with a terror registry attached

key_facts.fact: Argentina's government sent Congress a National Sovereignty Defense Bill on Thursday, September 17, which Milei presented as "a milestone in the process of recovering" the Falklands.
key_facts.excerpt: Argentina's government sent Congress a National Sovereignty Defense Bill on Thursday, presented by President Javier Milei as "a milestone in the process of recovering" the Falklands

key_facts.fact: The bill replaces the 2011 Law 26,659 and extends penalties from hydrocarbons to any natural resource on the Argentine continental shelf; barred companies could lose the right to operate anywhere in Argentina.
key_facts.excerpt: replaces Law 26,659, in force since 2011, and broadens its scope: no longer just hydrocarbons, but any natural resource, renewable or not, on the Argentine continental shelf... Companies that are barred would risk being unable to operate anywhere in the country

key_facts.fact: It creates a National Security Council chaired by Milei that can order urgent measures — restricting FX and financial operations, freezing assets, suspending contracts and restricting foreign trade — and lets the armed forces protect strategic facilities.
key_facts.excerpt: The bill creates a National Security Council, chaired by Milei, empowered to order "urgent measures" in the face of a grave and imminent threat: restricting foreign exchange and financial operations, temporarily freezing funds and assets, suspending authorizations or contracts, and restricting foreign trade.

key_facts.fact: Its most contested element is a public registry of people linked to terrorism (RePET), run by the Financial Information Unit, where inclusion requires only "reasonable grounds for suspicion" and no prior criminal case, triggering immediate asset freezes.
key_facts.excerpt: Inclusion in the registry "will not be conditioned on the existence of a criminal case": "reasonable grounds for suspicion" of a link to terrorism suffice, or a designation by the UN Security Council. The measure immediately triggers the freezing of funds and assets

key_facts.fact: Hours before the bill reached Congress, a federal judge in Tierra del Fuego ordered Rockhopper Exploration and Navitas Petroleum to halt work on the 23-well Sea Lion project on environmental grounds.
key_facts.excerpt: federal judge Mariel Borruto, of Río Grande, Tierra del Fuego, had granted an injunction... The judge ordered Rockhopper Exploration and Navitas Petroleum Development and Production to refrain from starting or continuing work on the Sea Lion project, which envisions 23 wells

key_facts.fact: Milei said the Falklands strategy had been in the works for three years and was triggered by Trump's remark about reviewing US neutrality in the dispute, rejecting claims it is electioneering before the 2027 vote.
key_facts.excerpt: "Political analysts say we pushed Malvinas for image reasons and political opportunism. That's a massive stupidity," he said, adding that the strategy had been in the works for three years and that the trigger was a remark by US President Donald Trump about reviewing his country's neutral stance in the dispute.
